title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 51-53, section 7): Grothendieck classifies the 'MD-graphes' G, i.e. the dual graphs of stable ν-pointed curves with vertex genera g_α and marked-point weights ν_α. The aim is to describe the strata M̂_G of the boundary of M̄_{g,ν} whose dimension is ≤ 2. The previous page treats maximal graphs, those of dimension 0. For these, every vertex has genus 0 and ν_α = 3 − ω_α, where ω_α is the valence. Then M_G ≅ Spec Z = S_0 and M_[G] ≅ B(Γ_{S_0}) with Γ = Aut G. This is the classifying stack of the constant group, i.e. the stacky point.

Formula (62) gives a variant for a modified group Γ^!: (M_[G], Γ^!) ≅ B(Γ^!_{S_0}).

The page then defines the 'ambient modular dimension' of a maximal MD-graph. It is the dimension of the moduli space M_{g,ν} in which the graph lives: dim_mod(G) = 3(g−1)+ν. Since g = Σ g_α + h_1(G) and all g_α = 0 for maximal graphs, this equals 3(h_1(G)−1)+ν. It also equals card I, the number of edges, i.e. the number of nodes of the maximally degenerate curve.

Grothendieck enumerates the cases dim_mod ≤ 2. Since ν ≥ 0, this forces h_1 ∈ {0,1}.
(a) Case h_1 = 0, so G is a tree.
- dim = ν − 3, so 3 ≤ ν ≤ 5.
- A tree that is not topologically a point or a segment has at least 3 leaves. Each leaf has valence 1 and genus 0, so it carries weight 2. Hence ν ≥ 6, which is excluded.
- So G is a single vertex or a path. Endpoints carry weight 2 and interior vertices weight 1, so ν = k+2 for a path with k ≥ 2 vertices.
This gives the three cases (64), each drawn as the corresponding stable curve:
- a vertex of weight 3: ν = 3, dim 0, the point M_{0,3};
- 2—2: ν = 4, dim 1, a boundary point of M̄_{0,4} (two lines crossing, carrying a,b and c,d);
- 2—1—2: ν = 5, dim 2, a maximal-degeneration point of M̄_{0,5} (a chain of three lines carrying a,b; c; d,e).

The next page treats h_1 = 1 (dim = ν ≤ 2). It finds the 1-loop graph for M_{1,1}, plus the banana graph and the loop-with-tail for M_{1,2}. Altogether this lists the maximal degenerations of the five 'small' moduli spaces M_{0,3}, M_{0,4}, M_{0,5}, M_{1,1}, M_{1,2}. These are exactly those with 3g−3+ν ≤ 2: the building blocks of the Teichmüller tower in the Esquisse d'un programme (first two levels generate, dimension ≤ 2 gives relations).
errors: The equality 3(g−1)+ν = 3(h_1−1)+ν holds only when all vertex genera vanish. This is legitimate here because the graphs are maximal (condition d of the previous page), but the page states it without that qualification; the marginal 'puisque g = Σg_α + h_1' supplies the justification.
Minor: 'segment' must be read topologically (a path of any length). A combinatorial segment of length 1 would miss the 2—1—2 case, which he does list. No mathematical error in the enumeration.

ideas.what: Ambient modular dimension of a maximal stable graph, 3g−3+ν, equal to the number of edges and expressed via h_1 when vertex genera vanish
ideas.modern_name: dimension of M_{g,n}; number of edges of a trivalent stable graph (pants decomposition)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Deligne–Mumford, Knudsen; pants decompositions: Fenchel–Nielsen, Hatcher–Thurston)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (modular dimension of the Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: Enumeration of maximal degenerations (trivalent stable graphs) for modular dimension ≤ 2: M_{0,3}, M_{0,4}, M_{0,5}, M_{1,1}, M_{1,2}
ideas.modern_name: zero-dimensional boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} with 3g−3+n ≤ 2; Lego pieces of the Teichmüller tower

ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (two-level principle, dimension ≤ 2 objects)

ideas.what: Stacky point M_[G] ≅ B(Aut G) over Spec Z for a maximal degeneration, with a variant for a modified group Γ^!
ideas.modern_name: zero-dimensional boundary stratum as classifying stack BAut(G)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in stack theory of M̄_{g,n} (Deligne–Mumford, Knudsen)

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, routine graph-theoretic enumeration of the maximal degenerations for M_{0,3}, M_{0,4}, M_{0,5}, M_{1,1} and M_{1,2}. It matches the dimension-≤2 building blocks of the Esquisse d'un programme, which are well known. It is of historical interest as the working-out behind the two-level principle, but contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The insertion above the line reads 'ambiante"', so the phrase is 'La "dimension modulaire ambiante" d'un M_G est'.
The marginal note reads 'puisque g = Σ_α g_α + h_1' and is attached to (63).
'h_1 ≤ 1, i.e.' is written under 'cette dimension est ≤ 2' and precedes 'h_1 ∈ {0,1}'.
Figures at right: the first is a single line with points a, b, c; the second two crossing lines carrying a, b and c, d; the third a chain of three lines carrying a, b / c / d, e.
